subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy reviews a new Depo-Testosterone prescription. Select all conclusions supported by the canonical rules.

choices.text: A qualifying non-opioid Schedule III prescription may use the statutory 90-day single-fill pathway.
The drug is Schedule VI because it is a hormone.
Covered dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
The original may be refilled without regard to federal refill limits.
A Schedule II emergency oral follow-up prescription is required.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps. Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard. testosterone cypionate (Depo-Testosterone) is used for replacement therapy in males with conditions associated with deficient endogenous testosterone. It is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.
